coverage: Named roster: 'From Elfland to Poughkeepsie' fetched in full (PDF reprint); Steering the Craft partial (ch.1 in full at Literary Hub, ch.10 as a long verbatim quotation, ch.5's rule via a quotation page); The Language of the Night NOT fetched, reached only through Stan Carey's quotations of the 1989 revised edition (an edition variant recorded); The Wave in the Mind fetched in full as a 253-page PDF, giving both rhythm essays at the primary; Earthsea's own text in copyright and read only at second hand. Blocked: Paris Review Art of Fiction No. 221 (no live page, NO Wayback capture, archive.ph empty), Jo Walton's Farthest Shore post, Andrew Wille's review; kate_nepveu recovered via the Wayback raw capture. Not found: any stylometric study of Le Guin on this angle, and any game-designer craft essay on her prose - the nearest are Mythcreants (a storytelling-craft site serving RPG writers) and Story Grid (editor training); that thinness is itself the finding. 22 substantive sources of 29 read: 5 by the named roster fetched direct, 4 by bibliography chasing (Stan Carey and the source list of a discarded AI-assisted blog), 13 by lateral search. Discovery ended when the session's 200-call WebSearch budget was exhausted, not on the two-empty-searches rule.
